evals.prompt: I ran simplify after touching three files. Two duplicate private helpers are in the same file; another cleanup would require cross-module import changes. What is safe to apply directly versus ask-first?
evals.expected_output: A simplify baseline response that allows local safe cleanup and classifies cross-module refactors as ask-first.
expectations: Treats same-file private deduplication as a safe-path candidate
Treats cross-module import boundary changes as ask-first
Keeps scope anchored to recently changed files
Includes concise output summary structure: scope, applied changes, deferred ask-first items, validation

evals.prompt: I ran /simplify on my last commit and one of the reviewers flagged that a utility function in src/utils/format.ts is almost identical to one in src/helpers/string.ts. Both are used by different modules. The simplify flow classified this as ask-first rather than safe. Why would it do that and what should I do next?
evals.expected_output: An explanation of the safe-versus-ask-first boundary in simplify, why cross-module deduplication is ask-first, and what the next step is.
expectations: Explains the safe-versus-ask-first boundary: safe means local to scoped files while ask-first means cross-module or public API changes
Identifies cross-module deduplication as ask-first because it changes import paths and module boundaries for consumers
Recommends resolving the deduplication by choosing one canonical location and updating all consumers
Suggests creating a beads task or follow-up for the deduplication if it is too large to do inline
References the structured closing summary where deferred and ask-first items are listed

evals.prompt: I ran /simplify right after a tiny docs-only commit that just fixed punctuation, and it returned basically no actionable cleanup. Is that expected?
evals.expected_output: A simplify no-op response that confirms no-op is valid when there is no meaningful safe simplification and does not invent changes.
expectations: Acknowledges that no-op outcomes are acceptable when recent changes do not contain worthwhile simplifications
Avoids fabricating refactors just to satisfy the workflow
Keeps scope anchored to recently changed files and commit intent
Provides a brief completion summary even when no edits are made
Reflects standalone code-simplify ownership where command routing is thin and workflow semantics come from code-simplify references

evals.prompt: On my latest commit, two private helper functions in the same file parse the same JSON shape with slightly different error strings. If I run /simplify with focus on duplication cleanup, should that be treated as a safe-path change?
evals.expected_output: A simplify safe-path explanation that identifies local same-file deduplication as safe and keeps changes bounded.
expectations: Identifies same-file private helper deduplication as a typical safe-path candidate
Keeps edits bounded to recently changed scoped files without widening across modules
Explains why this differs from cross-module ask-first cases
Includes concise summary of what would be changed and why
